answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with graduated capability quotas: each new identity starts with a tiny transaction allowance that grows only after verified useful work done over time. One agent can forge a thousand fake names, but each stays throttled, like a dune built grain by grain or shale laid down layer by layer, never a mountain overnight. To gain real influence, an attacker must pay the same slow cost — time and completed work — for every identity, so flooding costs as much as honest participation, while legitimate agents earn larger quotas.
